gongshuilong:study:1.title: A new saurolophine hadrosaurid (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of South China, providing further support for the possible Asian origin of Brachylophosaurini (Journal of Systematic Palaeontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Gongshuilong is characterized by uniquely elongated and curved neural spines on its tail vertebrae that formed a tall, sail-like structure.
facts.quote: Gongshuilong is characterized by the uniquely elongated and curved neural spines of the vertebrae at the end of the tail, forming a tall, sail-like structure.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Gongshuilong's tail vertebrae were 8.5 times as tall as the vertebrae's central body and were slightly curved backward.
facts.quote: The neural spines of the posterior caudal vertebrae are greatly elongate, at 8.5 times as tall as the centrum they are attached to, and somewhat recurved.

facts.statement: The fossils of Gongshuilong were discovered in March 2021 during construction in Shahe, Ganzhou city, Jiangxi Province, China.
facts.quote: In March 2021, construction was underway for the East China International Trade and Industrial Zone in the town of Shahe in Ganzhou city, Jiangxi Province, China.

facts.statement: Gongshuilong fanwei was formally described as a new genus and species by Han Yao and colleagues in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Han Yao and colleagues described Gongshuilong fanwei as a new genus and species of brachylophosaurin hadrosaurid based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The species name fanwei refers to the prominent sail-like tail morphology of the dinosaur.
facts.quote: The specific name, fanwei, is another pinyin term alluding the prominent sail-like tail morphology that characterizes this species.

facts.statement: Gongshuilong lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) in China.
facts.quote: Gongshuilong () is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) Lianhe Formation of China.

facts.statement: Gongshuilong lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gongshuilong is the first named hadrosaurid discovered in South China.
facts.quote: It is also the first hadrosaurid to be named from fossils found in South China.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Gongshuilong as a member of the tribe Brachylophosaurini within the clade Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: They recovered Gongshuilong as a member of the tribe Brachylophosaurini within the hadrosaurid clade Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: The exact evolutionary relationships within the Brachylophosaurini tribe remain unresolved, with Gongshuilong forming a polytomy with Wulagasaurus, Acristavus, and other North American genera.
facts.quote: The analysis found an unresolved polytomy within this clade, comprising Gongshuilong, Wulagasaurus, Acristavus, and a clade comprising Maiasaura, Brachylophosaurus, and Probrachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Gongshuilong contains only one species, G. fanwei, known from a bonebed containing at least two individuals.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Gongshuilong fanwei, known from a bonebed representing the disarticulated remains of at least two individuals.
